name: warp_queue
kind: installation, timing: the per-warp queue of 10 behind mio_throttle / lg_throttle -- admission at issue, serial release with an interval per kind and width, class of the wait, stores taking a turn in the shared-memory return chain; the per-SMSP global store interval is removed. The SM-level rates are not in this step.
mechanisms: instruction.service (new queue fields on STS, LDS, SHFL.IDX, SHFL.BFLY, LDG, STG rows; STS joins return chain 1)
evidence: queue_basic v1 and v2 addenda (readings), mem_basic v1 addenda, mio_basic r3 (SHFL.BFLY). Both devices alike; every number below is from those readings.

rules.Q1 members: An issued instance of STS, LDS, SHFL.IDX, SHFL.BFLY, LDG or STG (any width; not predicated off; not a remote shared-memory access) is an entry of its warp's queue from its issue until its release. No other instruction is a member (S2R, MUFU, LDC, S2UR, LDL, STL, SHFL.UP / .DOWN, atomics, TMA: no evidence or evidence against).
rules.Q2 release: Per warp one release server with a free time F (fractions kept). Entry j with release interval r_j, issued at cycle i_j: start_j = max(F, i_j + 5.5 + 0.5 r_j); release_j = start_j + r_j; F = release_j. r: LDS 2 (all widths); SHFL.BFLY 2; STS and STS.U8 / .U16 4; SHFL.IDX 4; LDG 4 (all widths); STG of at most 32 bits 6; STS.64 8; STG.64 8; STS.128 10; STG.128 12.
rules.Q3 admission: A member cannot issue while 10 entries of its warp are unreleased; it waits at issue until the oldest of them is released (whole-cycle view: the first cycle at or after that release). Ledger reason of the wait: warp_queue:lg when the waiting instruction is LDG or STG and all ten unreleased entries are LDG / STG, otherwise warp_queue:mio; mapped to lg_throttle and mio_throttle (calibrated, this protocol).
rules.Q4 stores in the return chain: STS (every width) takes a turn in its warp's return chain 1 (the chain of S2R / LDS / SHFL of mio_basic v4) with the chain interval equal to its r of Q2, so that a load behind stores returns later by the stores' intervals. Nothing else about the chain, its SM service ports or the in-flight groups changes; LDG / STG do not enter it.
rules.Q5 global store interval: storage.global.store_issue (per-SMSP interval 3 / 6 / 23 cycles by width) is disabled on both devices: the hardware issues ten stores one cycle apart. The per-SM store-buffer gate stays as it is until the SM step.
rules.not in this step: SM-level rates (one per cycle for STS / LDS / LDG / SHFL.IDX, the store rate by lines), result time of global loads behind global stores, the wide-slot LDS's slow results, the four-line 4-byte store's 7.6.

hand derivation before freezing: One warp, issue one per cycle from cycle 0 (the replay's producers), release times by Q2. STS run: 11.5, 15.5, ...: producer 11 (index 10) waits 1.5 (hardware 1.1 / 1.0), later ones 3.0 (2.93-2.99). STG: 14.5 + 6 j: 4.5 then 5.0 (4.0 / 4.0, 4.95). LDS: 8.5 + 2 j: producer 14 waits 0.5 then 1.0 (1.1, 0.98). q.seq.sts6_lds18: releases 11.5 ... 31.5 (STS), 33.5, 35.5 ... (LDS): producer 11 waits 1.5, 12-16 3.0, 17 on 1.0 (hardware 1.1 / 1.0; 2.4-3.5; 0.7-1.2). q.seq.lds12_sts12: 8.5 ... 30.5, 34.5, 38.5: producer 13 waits 0.5 (0.0 / 0.0), 14-22 1.0, 23 and 24 3.0 (3.1, 2.7 / 2.8, 3.3). q.alt.sts_stg (r 4, 6 alternating): releases 11.5, 17.5, 21.5, 27.5 ...: behind the onset STS waits 3.0 and STG 5.0 (3.02 / 3.08, 4.93 / 5.00). Class: sts10_stg6 the STG wait behind STS entries: warp_queue:mio (hardware mio_throttle); stg6_ldg18 all global: lg; alt cells mixed: mio. Q4, q.fwd.sts<M>_lds2: chain turns of the stores at 0, 4, ... 4 (M - 1), of the two LDS at 4 M and 4 M + 2, result 22 after the turn: reader wait 4 M + 24 - (M + 2) = 3 M + 22: 22, 28, 34, 46 (hardware 23.0, 30.2, 36.0, 47.7 / 22.8, 29.7, 33.1, 47.0). q.lds.n24: the chain is as today, the producers now wait 11 at issue, so the reader's wait falls from 44.7 / 43.7 to about 33.7 / 32.7 (hardware 34.2 / 34.2). Cells with n24 / n28 or rate cells carry a backlog from one iteration into the next and are not derived by hand; the replay decides.

criteria.K1 (one warp, per kind): For the one-warp cells of queue_basic v1 and v2 whose producers are members (v1: q.sts / stg / ldg / lds / shfli runs, the six wide-store runs, q.lds128.n12, q.ldg128.n12, the four depth sequences, the membership sequences without MUFU, q.stg.e2 / e3 / e4 / e6, q.stg16.e3, q.stg16_f2fp.e3, q.stgd.n16, q.stgfar.n8 / n16, q.sts.e2 / e3; v2: the seven q.alt cells, q.stg8.e3) on both devices: (a) the loop total is within 3 % of the hardware's (pass a); (b) per producer kind the summed wait at issue is within max(2.0, 10 %) of the hardware's and carries the hardware's class (mio_throttle or lg_throttle) as its largest class; (c) the cell's (pc, class) error is at most 0.30.
criteria.K2 (depth, per pc): q.seq.sts6_lds18: producers 12-16 each wait at least 2.0, producers 17-24 at most 1.6; q.seq.lds12_sts12: producers 14-22 at most 1.6, 23 and 24 at least 2.0; q.seq.stg6_ldg18: producers 12-16 at least 4.0, 17-24 between 2.4 and 3.6.
criteria.K3 (readers of shared loads): reader wait within 3.0 of the hardware's in q.lds.n24, q.lds.n28, q.shfli.n24, q.fwd.sts0_lds2, .sts2_lds2, .sts4_lds2, .sts8_lds2, q.alt.sts_lds.n24, q.seq.sts6_lds18, q.seq.sts10_shfli6.
criteria.K4 (untouched cells): Every cell of every probe source (manifest-queue1 plus queue_basic-v2) whose kernel has no member instruction and no STG / ST store has a ledger identical to the b046ee5c replay's (cycles and every residency row). In particular q.nop*, q.s2r.n28, q.mufu.*, q.f2fp.n8.
criteria.K5 (no harm elsewhere, per pc and class): Over all cells of all probe sources: the (pc, class) error does not rise by more than 0.05 in any cell; every cell that does is listed with its per-pc table and a cause. The multi-warp cells of queue_basic are reported, not judged (SM step).
criteria.gates and runs: seven gates on a clean clone; replay of every probe source; full GPU 500 x 2 with ledgers; multi-level comparison against compare/mufu1 with the noise floor. Full-GPU numbers are reported, MAPE as reference; no full-GPU number is a criterion.

expectation_not_criterion: Full GPU: mio_throttle rises on STS / LDS pcs and lg_throttle on LDG pcs (hardware 0.24 + 0.13 + 0.04 points on H100 against 0 in the replay), short_scoreboard at readers behind stores rises; cycles of kernels with long store runs move; with the store interval gone STG-heavy epilogues get faster at one warp per SMSP and the per-SM store buffer still dominates saturated stores.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or the literature; no full-GPU case or error used to choose a rule or a value; a criterion that fails is recorded as failed.

addenda.when: 2026-11-22, before any replay with the rules (no data)
addenda.text: Two points of the criteria fixed before data. (1) K4 as worded has an almost empty set and names cells that are not in it: every probe kernel stores its results with STG and the q / m2 frames have member instructions in front of and behind the loop (anchors), so 'whose kernel has no member instruction and no STG / ST store' excludes q.nop, q.s2r.n28, q.mufu.* and q.f2fp.n8 as well. K4 is judged in this form instead: for every cell of every source whose loop pcs hold no member instruction and no STG / ST / STL, (a) one warp per SM: the ledger's residency rows on the loop pcs and the pc behind the loop are identical to the b046ee5c replay's, reason by reason; (b) several warps per SM: the loop total differs by at most 0.5 % (the prologue's stores can shift the warps against each other), every larger difference is listed. The literal K4 is reported too (number of kernels without any member or store, and whether their ledgers are identical). (2) K1 (b)'s class clause applies to a producer kind when the hardware's largest wait class on that kind is mio_throttle or lg_throttle with at least 1.0 cycles per iteration; where the hardware has no such wait the clause has nothing to compare and only the amount is judged. K1's cell list in full: v1 q.sts.n16 / n24 / n28, q.stg.n16 / n24 / n28, q.ldg.n16 / n24, q.lds.n24 / n28, q.shfli.n24, q.sts8.n24, q.sts64.n24, q.sts128.n24, q.stg16.n24, q.stg64.n24, q.stg128.n24, q.lds128.n12, q.ldg128.n12, q.seq.sts6_lds18, q.seq.lds12_sts12, q.seq.stg6_ldg18, q.seq.ldg12_stg12, q.seq.sts10_shfli6, q.seq.sts10_lds128x6, q.seq.sts10_ldg6, q.seq.sts10_stg6, q.seq.stg10_sts6, q.seq.stg10_lds6, q.seq.ldg10_sts6, q.stg.e2 / e3 / e4 / e6, q.stg16.e3, q.stg16_f2fp.e3, q.stgd.n16, q.stgfar.n8 / n16, q.sts.e2 / e3; v2 q.alt.sts_lds.n24, q.alt.stg_ldg.n24, q.alt.sts_stg.n24, q.alt.lds_ldg.n24, q.alt.stg_lds.n24, q.alt.sts_stg.n16, q.alt.lds_ldg.n16, q.stg8.e3 (48 cells per device). Known before data and not hidden: the rules do not model the result time of global loads behind stores, the wide-slot loads or the four-line store, so K1 (a) / (c) may fail on q.seq.stg6_ldg18, q.alt.stg_ldg, q.lds128.n12, q.ldg128.n12, q.seq.sts10_lds128x6; they stay in the list.

addenda.text: Verdict: K2 and K4 pass on both devices, K1 fails on both, K3 passes on H100 and fails on one cell on B300, K5 fails on one cell on H100. The rules stay on the branch because every failing cell fails on something these rules do not contain and none is made worse beyond K5's one cell; they are not sufficient and v2 follows. Details. Replay: 14 of 15 sources complete per device; mem_basic reports its four ldgfar cells, which have no capture. K1 (49 cells per device; the addendum's '48' was a miscount of its own list): 24 pass on H100, 34 on B300. The shared-memory side passes everywhere it is alone: q.sts.n16 / n24 / n28, q.sts8, q.sts64, q.sts128, q.lds.n24 / n28, q.shfli.n24, q.seq.sts6_lds18, q.seq.lds12_sts12, q.seq.sts10_shfli6, q.sts.e2 / e3, q.alt.sts_stg (both), and on B300 also every 4-byte STG cell. Failures in three groups. (i) Global stores where the SM's store-buffer gate bites at one warp -- H100 every STG cell (q.stg.n16 total 130.0 against 116.0: store_buffer 27.6 on top of warp_queue:lg 15.1 where the hardware has lg_throttle 28.7 in all; the same excess as before this step), both devices the 8- and 16-byte stores (786.6 / 431.5 against 190.7 / 190.0). (ii) Results of global loads: q.ldg.n16 / n24 (158.9 / 147.3 against 167.2 / 168.5: the producers' wait is right, 16.8 against 15.8, the reader is short), q.seq.stg6_ldg18, q.seq.sts10_ldg6, q.alt.stg_ldg, q.alt.lds_ldg, q.alt.stg_lds, q.seq.stg10_lds6. (iii) The wide-slot loads q.lds128.n12, q.ldg128.n12, q.seq.sts10_lds128x6. (ii) and (iii) were named before the data in part; q.ldg.n16 / n24 were not. K2 PASS (the depth sequences per producer). K3: H100 10 of 10 readers within 3.0; B300 9 of 10 (q.alt.sts_lds.n24 41.0 against pass a's 47.9; pass b has 43.9). K4 PASS: 78 one-warp cells without a member in the loop have identical loop rows, 108 multi-warp cells within 0.5 % (4 / 3 differ at all); no kernel is without any member or store, so the literal K4 is empty. K5: H100 q.stg.n28 0.517 -> 0.570 (group (i): the queue's wait now adds to the store buffer's); B300 none; reported multi-warp cells q.sts.n10.w16 0.582 -> 0.692, q.sts.e3.w16 1.057 -> 1.109, q.mufu.e4.w16 0.639 -> 0.690 on B300. Full GPU against compare/mufu1 (H100 / B300): cycles change in most cases by little (MAPE 10.67 -> 10.76 % / 9.76 -> 9.77 %; H100 224 faster, 146 slower); attribution 0.3306 -> 0.3287 / 0.3232 -> 0.3225, class 0.3122 -> 0.3105 / 0.2904 -> 0.2895, (site, class) 0.4397 -> 0.4385 / 0.4348 -> 0.4341, (pc, class) 0.6996 -> 0.6986 / 0.7438 -> 0.7432, site 0.2527 -> 0.2532 / 0.2507 -> 0.2507, pc 0.5809 -> 0.5808 / 0.6271 -> 0.6268; the loops' mio_throttle gap does not move (-1.08 / -0.24 points), lg_throttle +0.30 -> +0.26 / +0.03 -> +0.01. The expectation that mio_throttle would rise on STS / LDS pcs did not hold: a per-warp queue alone does not saturate in the full-GPU kernels; by the queue_basic readings the wait there needs the SM's one-per-cycle limit (many warps), which is the next step. Read out of this run and the queue_basic tables for v2: the result of a member load follows its slot's release by a constant -- LDS and SHFL.IDX release + 14.2-15.2 (q.fwd.sts0_lds2, .sts8_lds2, q.lds.n24, q.shfli.n24), LDG release + 27.5-29.5 on H100 and 30.2 on B300 (4, 8, 16, 24 loads, and the alternation with LDS: 78.5 + 29.5), which also accounts for queue_basic v2's unexplained reader behind LDS ; LDG.
